The ideal true-motion fixture uses 4000 mm/s^2 because an ideal 5000 mm/s^2 sample is already above the unchanged 0.5 g impact threshold; this is a synthetic design choice, not a requested printer retune.
validation_reason: One final combined offline run after independent review. Configured batch backends use finite baseline_noise_floor in [0, 0.2] g (default 0.2); native Beacon keeps the original 20% quiet gate and raw motion/pressed decisions. Only accepted configured references exceeding the old 20% gate receive conservative uncertainty bounds for movement proof and automatic direction. A floor-only experiment reproduced false parked motion proof; the final correction rejects modeled balanced/slow/asymmetric parked bias without changing raw impact, thresholds or startup deadlines. Fixtures include true 50 mm/s ramps at 4000 mm/s^2 in both directions and clock epochs, first +/-0.51 g contacts after uncertain raw speed exceeds 30 mm/s, first/odd sample integration counts, safe low-speed no_motion, 0.21 g rejection and original timestamp/enable guards. All traces are synthetic, not a recording of a user device. Existing 0.5 g calibration start, strict ten-home <1.5 mm repeatability and configured-speed preservation remain unchanged.

quiet_baseline_diagnostics.gate_change_scope: Configured batch sensors below 1 g only; native Beacon gate unchanged.

quiet_reference_peak_to_peak_limit_scope: Configured sensors at the default 0.5 g calibration candidate use max(20% of the active threshold, baseline_noise_floor); native Beacon retains 0.1 g at 0.5 g. Thresholds at least 1 g retain the previous quiet limit.
baseline_noise_floor_scope: Configured batch accelerometers only; setting 0 restores the previous 20% rule. Native Beacon admission and motion/pressed behavior are unchanged.

expanded_reference_motion_proof.scope: Configured batch references whose actual accepted per-axis peak-to-peak exceeds the original 20% gate.
expanded_reference_motion_proof.automatic_direction: Select only when the signed velocity uncertainty interval is entirely beyond +30 mm/s or -30 mm/s; otherwise retain bidirectional impact detection.
expanded_reference_motion_proof.insufficient_low_speed_evidence: Fails existing no_motion policy; no automatic speed/acceleration edit
